theme.title: The ATL uprising
theme.subtitle: Atlanta Hawks, 2014–15
theme.recap: A balanced Atlanta team went unbeaten in January, won a franchise-record 60 games and claimed the East's top seed.

questions.prompt: How many regular-season games did the 2014–15 Hawks win?
questions.note: 60 wins, a franchise best and the East's top seed.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: 60–22 record for a franchise high in wins

funFacts.text: Atlanta's division crown was its first since it competed in the Central Division in 1994.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: first for the Hawks since winning the Central Division in 1994

funFacts.text: It was the first Southeast Division title won by a team outside Florida.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: division title was not won by a team from the state of Florida

funFacts.text: The Hawks reached the Eastern finals for the first time in the league's two-conference era.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: their first-ever Conference finals since the NBA was split into two conferences

questions.prompt: How many games did the 2015 Hawks win in an undefeated January?

funFacts.text: Atlanta stayed perfect both at Philips Arena and away from home during January.
The month closed with a home victory over Philadelphia.
The Hawks entered January at 23–8 and exited at 40–8.

Teague paced Atlanta's scoring against Memphis in a January home win.

funFacts.text: Atlanta was the first No. 1 seed swept in a playoff series since Detroit in 2003.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
